title: Level-one Fourier weight bound
statement: For every real $\alpha$ with $0<\alpha<1/2$, there is a constant $C_\alpha>0$ such that the following holds for every integer $n\ge0$. Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\le f(x)\le1$ for every $x$, have uniform-cube mean at most $\alpha$, and have each first-level Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon\ge0$. Then the sum of the squares of its first-level Fourier coefficients is at most $I(\alpha)^2+C_\alpha\varepsilon$, where $I(\alpha)$ is the standard Gaussian density evaluated at the real number whose standard Gaussian upper-tail probability is $\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is real-valued on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the uniform-cube mean of $f$ is at most $\alpha$
each first-level Fourier coefficient has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$
